context: Decide which is true and make the contract and the tooling agree: either implement 'doctor' as a real preflight on the project wrapper (and/or expose 'batch'), or amend the batch contract so its preflight names a check that actually exists here. Do not leave a mandated gate that no operator can execute.
description: The todo-db batch workflow requires a 'doctor' preflight before batch execution, but no reachable CLI implements it. Confirmed by enumeration, not by a failed lookup: '_project/scripts/todo --help' lists init, import-yaml, create, show, claim, release, renew, deps, unblock, start, done, defer, promote, dismiss, complete, drop, block, list, ready, stats, check-scope, verify, lint, sweep-stale, migrate, config, freeze, export, finding -- there is no 'doctor', and no 'batch' either. So the mandated preflight cannot be run by anyone following the contract, and sessions record it as 'skipped', which quietly converts a required gate into an optional one. Also note 'update' is absent from this wrapper (standalone-only), which is what makes malformed verification ladders unrepairable in place and forces drop+recreate under a new id.

preserves.behavior: No change to the standalone-only command boundary: standalone-only actions must still not be routed to the project wrapper

verifications.description: the project wrapper exposes the mandated preflight
the batch contract no longer names an unavailable preflight, or batch is itself exposed
